speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear your baby is unwell; tell me, did the vomiting contain bile, which would look green or yellow? Also, has the baby passed any stool since birth, or is there a history of abdominal distension?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium in a newborn, I am concerned about a distal intestinal obstruction. Did the pregnancy have a known history of polyhydramnios? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray (supine and upright).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-Ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
